Assign Per-Class LOS RR to Resistance Profiles (Max Rule)

Source: R/daly_rr_and_los.R
daly_assign_rr_to_profiles.Rd

For each resistance profile delta, determines the profile-level relative LOS using the GBD max rule: RR_kd_LOS = max over c in C_R(d) of RR_kc_LOS [if C_R(d) non-empty] = 1 [if d = all-susceptible] where C_R(d) is the set of classes the profile is resistant to. The class attaining the maximum is the profile's dominant class d*. The CI reported for each profile is that of its dominant class.

Usage

daly_assign_rr_to_profiles(
  profiles_output,
  rr_table,
  pathogen_col = "pathogen",
  class_col = "antibiotic_class",
  rr_col = "RR_LOS",
  fallback_rr = 1,
  los_r_col = NULL,
  los_s_col = NULL,
  los_unit = c("years", "days"),
  profile_col = "profile_delta",
  profile_probability_col = "R_mean",
  profile_hospital_col = "group",
  profile_classes_col = "classes",
  profile_class_order = NULL
)

Arguments

profiles_output

Legacy list from compute_resistance_profiles() or a data frame of profile strings (see "Profile input formats").

rr_table

The list returned by daly_fit_los_rr(), or a data frame with columns pathogen_col, class_col, rr_col and optionally CI_lower / CI_upper (e.g. from daly_fit_los_rr_distribution()).

pathogen_col

Character. Pathogen column in rr_table (and in string profiles). Default "pathogen".

class_col

Character. Default "antibiotic_class".

rr_col

Character. Default "RR_LOS".

fallback_rr

Numeric. RR for resistant classes with no match. Default 1 (no attributable effect).

los_r_col, los_s_col

Character or NULL. Columns in a data-frame rr_table with absolute LOS for resistant / susceptible patients (e.g. "median_LOS_R" / "median_LOS_S"). Ignored when rr_table is a daly_fit_los_rr() list.

los_unit

Character. Unit of los_r_col / los_s_col: "years" or "days". Default "years".

profile_col

Character. Profile-string column. Default "profile_delta".

profile_probability_col

Character. Profile probability column in string profiles. Default "R_mean". Copied to probability.

profile_hospital_col

Character or NULL. Hospital column in string profiles. Default "group"; NULL or absent means pooled profiles. Copied to hospital.

profile_classes_col

Character. Column of string profiles holding the class order as one ;-separated string. Default "classes".

profile_class_order

NULL (read the order from profile_classes_col), a character vector (the class of each letter, in order) or a named list of such vectors, one per pathogen.

Value

Named list (one entry per pathogen): the profiles data frame augmented with RR_LOS_profile, dominant_class, (if available) CI_lower_profile / CI_upper_profile, LOSR_years / LOSS_years, and for string profiles probability, hospital and los_level.

Details

Ties: when several resistant classes share the maximum RR, the first of them in the class order wins (profile_class_order for string profiles, the classes element for legacy profiles). A message reports how many profiles had a tie.

If rr_table was fit with a syndrome_name filter, its RR values are syndrome-specific but get applied here to all profiles of a pathogen – i.e. it assumes syndrome-invariant LOS prolongation.

Profile input formats

Legacy

The named list from compute_resistance_profiles() ($profiles with 0/1 class columns and $classes).

Profile strings

A data frame with one row per (hospital x) pathogen x profile, where the profile is a string of R/S letters such as "RRSR" – e.g. the output of profile_aggregate_for_daly() (group, pathogen, profile_delta, R_mean), or a burden table with hospital, pathogen, profile, mean and classes. When the default column names are absent, those of the burden table are used.

Class of each letter

The class order is read from profile_classes_col (e.g. "Fluoroquinolones;Aminoglycosides;Carbapenems"), which must hold a single value per pathogen. profile_class_order can be given instead, or to override it (a warning is raised if they differ). Class names are matched to the LOS results ignoring case and punctuation, so "Third_generation_cephalosporins" matches "Third-generation-cephalosporins".

LOS for each profile

When rr_table is the list returned by daly_fit_los_rr(), the profile takes the adjusted LOS of its dominant class: from rr_table$hospital for the profile's own hospital when the profiles carry a hospital column (los_level = "hospital"), otherwise the all-hospital values in rr_table$rr (los_level = "network"). Days are converted to years. With a data-frame rr_table, absolute LOS is taken from los_r_col / los_s_col as before. LOSR_years / LOSS_years are NA for the all-susceptible profile, which has no dominant class.

Two options for profile-level LOS

This function is option 2: per-class LOS estimates mapped to profiles by the max rule. Option 1 is daly_fit_los_distn_by_profile() (Section 5.3), which estimates LOS directly for each patient-level resistance profile against the fully susceptible profile.
